source.note: The source is this repository's own Python implementation, not a second checkout. Cadenza is being rewritten in place (cadenza#8): `src/cadenza/` and `tests/` are the specification until a later PR retires them, so every inventory here is collected from the working tree at the recorded revision.

suite_baseline.reconciliation: `PYTHONPATH=src PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` at a5672f8 on CPython 3.12.3: 330 passed. file.note: 6 test functions, 25 collected node ids: three of the six are parametrized, contributing 6, 11 and 5 cases.

systematic_mappings.why: The helper the compose and resolve ledgers already record. `expect(...).toThrow(Kind)` checks the class and `toThrow(/re/)` the message, but neither yields the INSTANCE, and one case goes on to assert `.location`. `match=` searches `str(exc)`, and `.message` here carries the same formatted text (`src/domain/errors.ts`), so the two see the same string.
systematic_mappings.affects: every refusal case: 11 shape refusals, 5 type refusals, and 3 more

systematic_mappings.why: TypeScript has no keyword-only parameters. The order is the source's declaration order and `location` keeps its default of nothing, spelled `null` rather than `None`.

pytest's node id is taken VERBATIM rather than derived from a title template (D-0010), so a target id is a function of the source id. That includes the two spellings pytest invents: the ASCII escape `web\xe9` for a non-ASCII parameter, and the fallback `value3`/`value4` for a list and a dict it will not print.

The direct translation. What each one has to preserve is the answer `pythonTypeName` gives for it -- `NoneType`, `bool`, `list`, `dict` -- which is asserted for its own sake in `test/domain/python-semantics.test.ts`.

ids: test/domain/identifiers.test.ts::the identifier pattern's anchors and its refusal set > carries no flags, because 'm' would restore Python's '$'
test/domain/identifiers.test.ts::the identifier pattern's anchors and its refusal set > refuses whitespace on both sides of the isspace()/\s disagreement
target_only_tests.why: The two traps the kickoff (cadenza#8) named for this file, held open. Neither translates a source case, and neither could: `tests/test_identifiers.py` cannot state that a regex flag is absent when the language has no such flag, and it cannot state that a whitespace predicate is not consulted when `str.isspace()` is the only one there is. Both are properties of the PORT, created by translating into a language whose defaults differ, which is the same reason `test/domain/canonical-json.test.ts` exists. The first pins that `IDENTIFIER_PATTERN.flags` is empty and demonstrates what `m` would admit; the second pins that all six code points where `str.isspace()` and `/\s/` disagree are refused, in both directions, so a later rewrite of the gate from a positive class into a `\s` refusal cannot loosen it unnoticed.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: `test_refuses_non_string_values_naming_the_type` asserts only `must be a string, got` and stops before the type name its own title promises. All five cases stay green against an implementation that named every type `int`.
inherited_limitations.why: The source's own shape, kept rather than strengthened: a translation that asserts more than its source is no longer a measure of the source. It is not left uncovered -- `test/domain/python-semantics.test.ts` asserts `pythonTypeName` against `str`, `NoneType`, `bool`, `list`, `dict` and `float` directly, and records the one place the int/float collapse is load-bearing (`schema_version`, in `parity/compose.ledger.json`).

inherited_limitations.behaviour: The refusal text embeds `repr(value)` and no case in this file asserts it, so the `pythonRepr` gap `src/domain/python-text.ts` documents is invisible to all 25.
inherited_limitations.why: Measured rather than assumed (D-0020). Over every code point, the port's `repr` differs from CPython's on 963,033 of them -- every non-ASCII code point CPython considers non-printable, which it decides from the Unicode character database. The divergence begins at U+0080: the ASCII range is exact, and so is this file's one non-ASCII case, U+00E9 being printable. The gap is message-only and reaches nothing that a run persists.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: Six accepted shapes and eleven refused ones are examples, not an enumeration. No case in this file establishes that the two implementations agree on the values nobody wrote a case about.
inherited_limitations.why: What a translated test can do. The differential sweep behind D-0020 is what makes the stronger claim: 3,169 values -- every code point below U+0300 in four positions, the whitespace and format controls above it, the terminator shapes, both length boundaries and astral characters, plus a separate lone-surrogate probe -- are accepted or refused identically by CPython and the port, with zero disagreements.

Same assertion, both halves: `parse_identifier('web\n')` is refused and the pattern itself does not match. Adapted because the mechanism is where the trap lives. The source's end anchor is `\Z`; the port's is `$` with NO `m` flag, which anchors at the end of the input exactly as `\Z` does -- JavaScript's `$` only acquires Python's `$` behaviour under `m`. And `re.Pattern.match`, which anchors at the start on its own and returns a match object or `None`, becomes `RegExp.prototype.exec`, whose anchoring comes from the pattern's own `^`. Measured (D-0020): the same source under `m` accepts `web\n` -- and also `web\r`, `web\u2028` and `web\u2029`, three terminators Python's `$` does not break a line at. The target-only case in the same file holds the flag absent.

entries.target_id: test/domain/identifiers.test.ts::parse_identifier > error names the field and the location
entries.reason: Same assertion, all three parts: the error carries the location, names the field, and prints the location last. Adapted for the shape change `src/domain/errors.ts` records -- `str(caught.value)` in Python is the formatted text and `.message` is the bare one, and in the port those are `.message` and `.detail` -- so `str(caught.value).endswith(...)` becomes `caught.message.endsWith(...)`. Python's keyword-only `location=` becomes a positional third argument, TypeScript having no keyword arguments.

entries.target_id: test/domain/identifiers.test.ts::parse_identifier > identifier error is a catalog error
entries.reason: Same assertion about the same class relationship: an identifier refusal is reachable through the one base class (design doc section 7). Adapted because `issubclass` has no expression in TypeScript -- a class is a value and a type, and only the value carries a prototype chain -- so the question is asked of an instance with `toBeInstanceOf`, which walks exactly what `issubclass` walks. The same substitution `parity/resolve.ledger.json` makes for `test_not_found_is_not_a_catalog_error`.
